power.sourceNote: Hybrid system net output, published as 110 hp. The petrol engine alone makes 57 kW at 5,000 rpm and the traction motor 50 kW; those do not add up to the system figure, because the two peak at different points.

torque.sourceNote: Petrol engine torque, at 4,200 rpm. The traction motor makes 400 N-m from zero rpm, but engine and motor torque cannot be summed into one crankshaft figure, so only the engine figure is recorded here.

fuelEconomy.sourceNote: EPA combined 46 mpg (US) for the 2004 car, converted at 235.215 L-mi/100km-gal. This is the current EPA estimate: the methodology changed in 2008 and earlier cars were recalculated, so it is not the figure on the 2004 window sticker.

co2.sourceNote: EPA tailpipe CO2, 193.2 g/mi, converted at 1.609344 km/mi. On the European cycle the same car was rated 104 g/km; the two numbers describe different tests, not a disagreement.

batteryCapacity.sourceNote: 201.6 V nickel-metal-hydride pack of 28 modules, each six 1.2 V 6.5 Ah cells. The control system keeps the state of charge between roughly 40% and 80%, so about 0.4 kWh of that is usable.

dragCoefficient.sourceNote: Given in the article body for the Kammback body; Wikipedia in turn cites Motor Trend.

frontalArea.sourceNote: Derived, not published: the drag-coefficient list gives a drag area (CdA) of 6.24 sq ft = 0.580 m2 for the 2004 Prius, and dividing by the published Cd of 0.26 gives 2.23 m2. The site’s standing 0.85 x width x height approximation gives 2.19 m2 for the same car, so the two agree to within 2%.

bootVolume.sourceNote: EPA hatchback luggage volume, 16 cu ft, converted at 28.3168 L/cu ft. EPA measures a hatchback to the roof, so this is not comparable with a European seats-up boot figure.

weightDistributionFront.sourceNote: Published as a 60/40 front/rear split by NHTSA's Canadian Vehicle Specifications for the 2004 car, recorded here as the front fraction. The dynamics model would otherwise assume 0.62 for a front-drive car, so this replaces a layout average with the measured figure.
